questions.stem: What is the difference between bioaccumulation and biodegradation?

options.text: Bioaccumulation is a natural process, biodegradation is artificial
Bioaccumulation is the build-up of pollutants in organisms, while biodegradation is the breakdown of substances by microorganisms
Bioaccumulation only affects plants, biodegradation only affects animals

questions.explanation: Bioaccumulation is the build-up of pollutants (such as heavy metals or pesticides) in an organism's body over time because they cannot be excreted efficiently. Biodegradation is the breakdown of substances by microorganisms into simpler, harmless products. Substances that bioaccumulate are often those that resist biodegradation.
